metadata.title: Uncertainty Hyperbola — σₓ × σₚ ≥ ħ/2 (viz riff)
metadata.purpose: Riff critique of the vol1-uncertainty-hyperbola D3 simulation: encodings, interaction honesty, and pedagogy — not the physics.

beats.narration_text: Bonjour, Liam. I'm Liam, in for Bear. Someone asked Claude to build a visualization of the Heisenberg uncertainty principle — squeeze position, and momentum explodes. We have two panels, one slider, three buttons, and a hyperbola. Let's not teach the physics. Let's judge the viz.

props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.
output: ✓ two panels: position density + log-log hyperbola

beats.new_visual_element: ClaudeComposerAsk — cold open, Liam in for Bear, judging the viz not the physics

beats.narration_text: At rest: two panels. Left — a red Gaussian curve labeled Position density |ψ(x)|², x-axis in nanometers. Right — a log-log plot, dark diagonal line labeled σₓ–σₚ Hyperbola, a filled red dot sitting on it. Above both: one slider, width parameter a in nanometers; three buttons — Gaussian, ISW n=1, ISW n=5. A readout strip shows σₓ, σₚ, and their product ratio live.

The slider drives the Gaussian state. σₓ equals a over root two — make a larger, position smears out. σₚ equals one over root two a — momentum sharpens. Their product never budges: always ħ over two. The red dot rides the hyperbola as a moves, and the ratio stays 1.000 the entire sweep.

Here is what it gets right. Log-log axes transform σₚ equals ħ over two σₓ into a straight line of slope minus one — the power law reads visually, no algebra required. The red dot traces exactly that line during the slider sweep; the Gaussian never escapes the minimum uncertainty bound. And the ISW markers above the line show students that other states don't saturate it. Each pro is doing work.

Three problems. Click ISW n=1 or n=5, then drag the slider — nothing happens. The thumb moves, the number updates, the charts don't. No disabled state, no tooltip. A student will think the viz is broken, or walk away with the wrong mental model. Second: the σₚ readout label says eV/c — the code computes normalized ħ/nm values. Wrong unit, wrong by a factor of three. Third: ISW marker labels are nine pixels — illegible at playback resolution.

Let's recap with Claude. The log-log encoding is right — elegant geometry. The red dot earns its place. But the ISW slider is a silent lie, and the unit label is stale. Use this in your quantum mechanics course after covering Gaussian states. Wire the slider to the ISW well width L — that is the one fix that matters most.

artifactLines: Log-log encoding: straight line makes the trade-off read
Red dot on minimum: Gaussian saturation shown tactilely
ISW markers: states above the bound quantified
Silent slider: interaction lie when ISW is active
Stale unit label: eV/c on a ħ/nm readout

beats.new_visual_element: ClaudeVerdictArtifact — verdict card with bare recap lines

beats.narration_text: I have an Uncertainty Hyperbola simulation: a slider for Gaussian width parameter a and toggle buttons for Gaussian, ISW n=1, and ISW n=5. When ISW is selected, the slider does nothing — the ISW markers are hardcoded for L=1nm. Fix this: wire the slider to ISW well width L, recompute σₓ and σₚ for each n at that L, and shift the markers on the log-log hyperbola dynamically. Also fix the σₚ readout — it shows eV/c but should show ħ/nm. Preserve the two-panel layout and log-log axes.
